newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial and all-share indices finished at record highs in heavy volumes on Friday on continued positive sentiment, but the gold index tumbled to its lowest since March, 1993.
Dealers said hopes of an early interest rate cut and the easing of foreign exchange controls spurred the market to a firm finish albeit not as exciting as Thursday.

"The market was flat most of the day. It was taking a breather. There was no arbitrage opportunity in the industrial and all-shares as there was no big premium or discount to fair value," Dominic Rey, international dealer at Investec Securities, told Reuters.
The overall index finished up 8.5 points to a fourth consecutive high of 7,411.2 points, the industrial index gained 5.3 points to a second consecutive high of 8,747.6.

Gold shares were under the yoke of an ailing bullion price which pushed them below 1,000 for the first time in more than four years. "There is no action in golds. Nothing sustainable. They are a complete non-event," one dealer said.
The gold index ended down 13.6 points to 994.8 points. Platinum stocks, on the other hand, galloped forward as the higher platinum price boosted sentiment.
"The platinum price has firmed up to $421. We are relatively bullish on platinum stocks," Rey said.
Rusplats leapt 8.04 percent to 84 rand, Potgietersrust jumped 6.04 percent to 32.50 rand and Leplats advanced 7.78 percent to 485 cents.
The platinum index surged 334.3 points to a new year high of 5,497.9 points.
Next week, the market was expected to shrug off the country's latest relaxation of exchange controls as a positive outlook for interest rates supports the market's recent record-breaking gains.
But the unit trust quarter-end on Monday was seen possibly boosting prices as players massaged prices.

Near-term equity index futures gain 52 points at close boosted by a late rally in local bonds which finish at new 16-month low. Dealers said the market could be expecting a positive money supply figure.

Gold contracts were untraded on Friday as players stay away from them on a shaky bullion price. Dealers said no one wanted to be long on golds, but the fact that they were not traded could mean players felt the price was getting too low.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,867/90 from 6,828, the industrial contract was at 8,651/60 from 8,598 and the gold contract was untraded at 660/700 from 693.
